support.p: Long rectangular stone plaque, reconstituted from three contigous fragments.

layout.p: Text takes up the majority of the stone, with thin margins. Text is roughly centred on the stone.

handNote.p: Text is relatively neat (although larger text in the first ten lines is a little more uneven). Simple serifs.

history.provenance: Discovered in Spello, nearby to the theatre in 1733.

exemplum sacri rescripti
Imperator · Caesar · Flavius · Constantinus
Maximus Germanicus Sarmaticus Gothicus victor
triumphator · Augustus · et · Flavius · Constantinus
et · Flavius · Iulius · Constantinus · et · Flavius
Constans
omnia quidem quae humani gene
ris societatem tuentur pervigilium cu
rae cogitatione conplectimur sed pro
visionum nostrarum opus maximus
est ut universae urbes quas in luminibus provin
ciarum hac regionum omnium species et forma dis
tinguitur non modo dignitatem pristinam teneant
sed etiam ad meliorem statum beneficentiae nos
trae munere probeantur cum igitur ita vos Tusci
ae adsereretis esse coniunctos ut inistituto
consuetudinis priscae per singulas annorum vi
ces a vobis adque praedictis sacerdotes creentur
qui aput Vulsinios Tusciae civitatem ludos
schenicos et gladiatorum munus exhibeant
sed propter ardua monitum et difficultates iti
nerum saltuosas inpendio posceretis ut indulto
remedio sacerdoti vestro ob editiones cele
brandas Vulsinios pergere necesse non esset
scilicet ut civitati cui nunc Hispellum nomen
est quamque Flaminiae viae confinem adque con
tinuam esse memoratis de nostro cognomine
nomen daremus in qua templum Flaviae gentis
opere magnifico nimirum pro amplitudinem
nuncupationis exsurgeret ibidemque his
sacerdos quem anniversaria vice Umbria de
disset spectaculum tam scenicorum ludorum
quam gladiatorii muneris exhiberet manente
per Tusciam ea consuetudine ut indidem cre
atus sacerdos aput Vulsinios ut solebat
editionum antedictarum spectacula fre
quentaret precationi hac desiderio vestro
facilis accessit noster adsensus nam civi
tati Hispello aeternum vocabulum nomenque
venerandum de nostra nuncupatione conces
simus scilicet ut in posterum praedicta urbs
Flavia Constans vocetur in cuius gremio
aedem quoque Flaviae hoc est nostrae gen
tis ut desideratis magnifico opere pereici
volumus ea observatione perscripta ne ae
dis nostro nomine dedicata cuiusquam con
tagiose superstitionis fraudibus polluatur
consequenter etiam editionum in prae
dicta civitate exhibendorum vobis
licentiam dedimus scilicet ut sicuti
dictum est per vices temporis sollem
nitas editionum Vulsinios quoque non de
serat ubi creatis e Tusica sacerdotibus memo
rata celebritas exhibenda est ita quippe nec
veteribus institutis plurimum videbitur
derogatum et vos qui ob praedictas causas
nobis supplices extitistis ea quae inpen
dio postulastis impetrata esse gaude
bitis

div.p: Copy of the Sacred Rescript. Imperator Caesar Flavius Constantinus Maximus Germanicus Sarmaticus Gothicus Augustus, the victor, the triumphant, and Flavius Constantinus, and Flavius Iulius Constantinus and Flavius Contans. In our reckoning, we embrace all things which preserve the fellowship of mankind with unceasing care; but it is the greatest concern for our foresight that all cities, whose the appearance and form are distinguished among the ornaments of the provinces and of all the regions, should not only retain their former dignity, but should be advanced to a better status through the gift of our beneficence. Therefore, since you have asserted that you were joined to Tuscia in such a way that, by the arrangement of a former custom, each year in alternating turns priests are chosen by you and the aforementioned [Tuscians], priests who exhibit theatrical shows and games of gladiators at Volsinii, a city in Tuscia, but on account of the arduousness of the mountains and the difficulties of the wooded routes, you have urgently begged that through the grant of a remedy it not be necessary for your priest to travel to Volsinii for the sake of celebration of games; specifically [you request] that we grant to your city – which now has the name of Hispellum and which you report borders and is connected to the Flaminian road – a name taken from our family name, and in which a temple of the Flavian clan be built in an excessively grand fashion in accord with the greatness of its appellation; and that in the same place, this priest whom Umbria has provided in alternate years should offer a spectacle of both theatrical shows and gladiatorial games, while the same custom remains in Tuscia, that the priest created in that place should frequent the aforementioned spectacles at Volsinii, as was customary. Our assent has been willingly added to your request and your desire. For we have conceded to the city of Hispellum the eternal designation and venerable name of our appellation, specifically that in future the aforementioned city be called Flavia Constans, in whose embrace we wish to be erected in grand fashion a temple also of the Flavian clan, this is of our clan, but that this restriction is noted, that the temple dedicated to our name not be polluted with the deceits of any contagious superstition. Consequently, we also give you permission to exhibit games in the aforementioned city, specifically as – as has been said – in successive periods, the celebration of games also may not be forsaken at Volsinii when priests from Tuscia have been appointed, the aforementioned celebration must be held. In this way, not much will seem diminished from the institutions already in place, and you, who came to us as suppliants on account of the aforementioned causes, will take pleasure in those things you have obtained, which you so urgently demanded.
